candidates.statement: Let g be a complex simple Lie algebra and k a positive integer, the level. Let q = e iπ d(k+h∨), with h∨the dual Coxeter number and d the ratio of the square lengths of the long to the short root. Then the unitary coboundary weak Hopf algebra AW(g, q) induces a rigid braided tensor category structure on the module category of the affine vertex operator algebra Vgk. Furthermore we construct, via the Drinfeld twist method, a braided tensor equivalence between this category and the modular quantum group fusion category C(g, q) for all Lie types. candidates.statement: A (compatible) unitary coboundary weak quasi-Hopf algebra A is defined by the following data: a) A unital weak quasi-Hopf algebra A endowed with a C∗-algebra involution with an antipode (S, α, β) b) a ribbon structure (R, v) for A associated to (S, α, β) such that the ribbon element v ∈A is unitary, c) a unitary central square root w ∈A of v such that ε(w) = 1, S(w) = w, d) ˜A = Aop as quasitriangular weak quasi-bialgebras, e) R = Rw−1 ⊗w−1∆(w) is positive. candidates.statement: The semisimple ∗-algebra AW(g, q) := Nat(W) of natural transformations of W admits a natural structure of unitary compatible coboundary weak Hopf algebra derived from C(g, q) and W. Thanks to Theorem 29.4 in [10]–our version of Drinfeld-Kohno theorem–the Zhu algebras A(Vgk) become unitary coboundary weak quasi-Hopf algebras with a Drinfeld twist from AW(g, q), by our version of Drinfeld-Kohno theorem. This is summarized in the following section, and detailed in Sect. 33 of [10].

candidates.statement: These are the main new abstract results to obtain the complete braided tensor equivalence, and rely on key aspects of the discovery of quantum groups. In Sect. 11 we apply these theorems to complete to proof of part (d) of Theorem 3.1. In this case we work on the comparison between the two structures transported to the side of the quantum groups, AW(g, q), and we need knowledge on the generating property by the braid group between tensor powers of the fundamental representation, to apply our uniqueness theorem. C. PINZARI
